status: DRAFT by Claude, 2026-11-08. Not reviewed by the user or a domain expert. 'rules' are Claude's reading. What each indicator needs, and where each AML term is recorded (its typology data source), live in ontology/application/typology_requirements.ttl, and which table provides which source in mappings/transaction/tx_features.r2rml.ttl (all also our reading). The per-source 'available here' marks that used to be typed here are now derived by src/sources.py (and asked of Ontop by src/typology.py).
how_status_is_decided: src/indicators.py: an indicator is 'answerable' when every term the indicator needs (ontology/application/typology_requirements.ttl, merged into each entry as 'needs' by registry()) exists in the source vocabulary or has a data term under it in ontology/alignment/aml_data_alignment.ttl, 'partial' when some do, 'unanswerable' when none do. Rules named in 'data_rules' report 'cannot check' when violated, not 'does not hold'. Indicators with mode 'facts_only' get state 'facts_only' and a 'facts' block instead of held / not held.

indicators.text: Cyclical patterns in funds or asset transfers that ultimately revert to the same origin across multiple accounts or entities, lacking a legitimate business rationale.
not_checked: lacking a legitimate business rationale (only a Warning if a record claims one)

indicators.text: Frequent cross-border inter-bank transfers involving convoluted routing paths, including multiple hops in high-risk or offshore jurisdictions, lacking clear business justification.
indicators.shape_status: facts only: no threshold and no verdict (the typology gives no number for 'multiple hops'); the shape holds one data-availability rule
not_checked: cross-border (the data has no country; between banks is not cross-border)
reports: interbank_legs: legs with sameBank = false, out of the hops

indicators.text: Multiple intra-group and inter-company transfers with minimal or no supporting documentation or economic justification.
Repeated use of identical VAT invoices or tax reclaim documents across multiple transactions without evidence of corresponding goods or services.
Frequent formation or acquisition of legal entities with no apparent operational presence, coupled with repeated changes in beneficial ownership.
Significant discrepancies between reported trade volumes and actual business operations, such as low-activity companies handling disproportionately large transaction volumes.
not_checked: no declared operations; only a logarithm of the amount

indicators.text: Detectable circular trade patterns in shipping and invoicing records, including repetitive shipments of identical goods and mismatched invoice values or inconsistent documentation.
Frequent establishment and dissolution of trading entities, alongside repeated changes to account or ownership details, all lacking transparent operational explanations.
Regularly documented shipments or services appear in official records without any corroborating logistics or operational evidence, indicating potential phantom transactions.

origin_named.text: The candidate names the account where the funds start (the first leg's payer).

first_leg_starts_at_origin.text: The first leg starts at the origin account.

last_leg_returns_to_origin.text: The last leg ends at the origin account: the funds revert to where they started.

consecutive_legs_connect.text: Each leg pays from the account the previous leg paid to.

legs_in_time_order.text: Legs are in time order (kept by decision, not in the typology text).

at_least_2_accounts.text: The pattern involves more than one account (the typology says 'multiple accounts').

business_rationale_recorded.text: Warning only: a business rationale is recorded for the cycle. The data holds none, so this never fires here.

route_bank_known.text: Every leg says whether it stays within one bank; otherwise the between-bank count is not available.

rule_source_legend.text: close to the words of the indicator
rule_source_legend.added: a decision of this project, not in the typology
rule_source_legend.data: data availability, not a pattern rule
